body: ready for review - quick gate green on 6726c1b8 (the two software-GPU trace suites segfault only under parallel threads and pass with --test-threads=1; no ui code touched). Mutation checks M1-M7 all RED when deleted, GREEN when restored (table in the body). Effort: high, no escalation.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 6726c1b81185c1124f836a00abe1954fffafe8bd -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge** (no blockers).

**What looks good**
- The fallback is narrow: `slice()` only retries as a union when the plain read already returned `NonManifold` (`slice.rs`, `slice()`), so any mesh that sliced before is untouched and no golden can move.
- `closed_solids` (`slice_bodies.rs`) accepts only a soup whose every edge is used exactly once each way (closed, consistently wound) and whose every body has positive signed volume. Welded shared edges and faces, open bodies and inward cavity shells keep the refusal. A body that will not slice on its own returns its own error.
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in the new file. The weld uses a checked `i64` cell range, `saturating_add` and `u32::try_from`; the union-find indexes through `get`/`get_mut`. Non-finite or huge coordinates return `None`, which falls back to the refusal.
- The union of per-body sections is the correct section for stacked, touching and overlapping closed solids. Overlap resolves through the 2D boolean union, and a solid nested inside another is absorbed.
- `material_above_of` and `material_overhead_of` moved verbatim and are re-exported. The new `GenError::Model` wording is clearer. The decision record is present, no new `camcraft-*` dependency, no CHANGELOG edit, no snapshot or process-file change. `slice.rs` is 423 lines, down from 466.

**Local results (PR merged with current main, trial merge clean)**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-geometry --test slice_bodies` | 6/6 |
| `camcraft-motion --test islands_model_fault --test ruling` | 2/2 and 10/10 |
| `camcraft-app --test shared_face_bodies` | 4 passed, 1 ignored (heavy lane) |
| clippy `-D warnings`, geometry + motion + app, all targets | clean |

Old-code check: I replaced the fallback call in `slice()` with the plain refusal and re-ran `slice_bodies`. `stacked_solids_sharing_their_walls_slice_as_their_union`, `solids_touching_along_a_face_slice_as_one_outline` and `nanometre_seam_drift_still_reads_closed_solids` failed; the refusal-case tests still passed, as expected. I restored the file afterwards.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- Holds stated in the PR body, passed on here: the laid-flat S1 post still carries "finish envelope near move 2728: 0.0081 mm gouge, 4.5756 mm rest". The gouge is under the gate and the rest is the 3D Finish steep-wall behaviour, which the PR says also appears on body pairs that never needed the union. That is held, not passed silently. The as-imported generation test is `#[ignore]` for the heavy lane (about 15 min in debug) and needs running at the cut.
- The author reports `trace_composite` and `trace_parity` segfaulting under parallel threads and passing at `--test-threads=1`. The diff touches no ui or trace code; I did not run those suites.
- Cost: the fallback re-welds the whole soup for each plane that hits `NonManifold`, so a genuinely non-manifold mesh pays that cost on every plane before refusing. That is acceptable, since it only applies where the old code refused.

**Not exercised by me**
Mutation checks M2 to M7, the heavy as-imported test, the ui suites, the full batch gate, and any hand check on a real machine or in the GUI.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
